loop.observation: Cross-server regression tests reproduced an online shared runtime being projected offline and excluded from assignable agents: a five-minute heartbeat save window and one-minute reload cache exceeded the 45-second liveness timeout, and unrelated snapshot saves postponed unsaved daemon heartbeats. Concurrent forced membership reads also starved the heartbeat TryLock polling path until its request deadline, reproduced by the profile-read contention test.
loop.hypothesis: Fifteen-second save and reload windows, measured against each daemon's committed LastSeenAt rather than the global snapshot SavedAt, preserve cross-server availability while still coalescing hot heartbeats.
loop.execute: Restore both documented 15-second defaults, reject configured save-plus-reload windows at or above the runtime liveness timeout, and rebuild per-daemon committed heartbeat timestamps after successful snapshot saves and loads. Failed saves do not advance the committed heartbeat checkpoint. Local saves do not postpone the next cross-server reload. Put context-bound heartbeats and ordinary snapshot operations in the same blocking acquisition queue, retaining cancellation without polling or abandoned lock goroutines.
loop.evaluate: Shared-agent tests cover cold and cached readers, unrelated recent snapshot saves, online runtime display, the HTTP assignable list, and accepted assignment by another workspace member; existing heartbeat coalescing and meaningful-change tests remain required. Repeated workspace profile reads must not starve runtime heartbeats; a cancelled waiter must leave the operation lock reusable.
loop.retrospective: Persistence cost optimization must fit within the liveness deadline across writer and reader servers. Global snapshot freshness is not evidence that every daemon heartbeat was persisted; broader CQRS remains subject to the measured decision rules above.
